comment: Her own words set the order: "treat its confirmatory assay as the rank-1 shared workup" yet concensusite files that assay into the notes and hands rank-1 to a continued PFS-only anti-angiogenic. She is already on bevacizumab, so continuing it is not the harm; the harm is letting the guideline default outrank the sequencing she explicitly asked for, when the GIS result is what decides whether bev stands alone or earns a PARP partner. Honor her rank-1, then let the score pick the maintenance.

This is how you carry a patient who leans efficacy at 0.7 but drew a hard line on the marrow: conservative ranks niraparib for the efficacy, then gates it on an individualized starting dose plus serial CBCs and says plainly "absent that gating I would veto." That respects the "severe myelosuppression / febrile neutropenia" veto without pretending it forecloses the strongest oral all-comer option, which is the exact tradeoff she set. Her WBC of 3.5 means the gating is not optional, and conservative treats it that way.

Critic lands T-DXd at rank-5 relapse-only on the evidence, and her preferences put it in the same place for a reason worth naming: of the two HER2 options, T-DXd's headline toxicities are ILD and nausea, so it clears both vetoes, while disitamab vedotin's MMAE payload hits "additional peripheral neuropathy" and severe neutropenia at once and is disqualified outright. The brake on T-DXd is hers, not the data's: IV q3w plus 10-12% ILD runs against "oral or low-infusion-burden preferred", so it stays a confirmed-relapse option behind a re-stain, not something to launch now. Same rank as critic, carried on the patient's stated tradeoffs.

Risktaker ranks the most marrow-toxic agent on the board first (31% grade 3+ anemia, 28.7% thrombocytopenia against a baseline WBC of 3.5) and books the "severe myelosuppression / febrile neutropenia" veto as a dosing footnote to be managed. The 0.7 efficacy lean is real, but it does not dissolve a hard veto; that veto is hers to lift, not the board's to rank past on a subgroup HR she is betting on without a GIS. To risktaker's credit those same vetoes got disitamab vedotin rejected, so apply the standard consistently and let her, not the ranking, decide whether the marrow risk is acceptable.

No society endorses HER2-directed therapy for HER2-low ovarian cancer: the tumor-agnostic T-DXd approval requires IHC 3+, the ovarian cohort (pmid:37870536) enrolled 2+/3+, and the IHC 1+ data are all breast (pmid:35665782). Seating it at rank 5, above rucaparib, which NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 lists at category 2A as an all-comer PARP, inverts the consensus order for an investigational pick. You already named the confirmatory re-stain and a basket trial in your own rationale, and that is the guideline-aligned route for an off-guideline agent, not a ranked therapeutic seat.

We agree letrozole is the gentlest option here and clears both named vetoes, and NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 does list hormone therapy in this disease. But the panel does not grade aromatase-inhibitor maintenance at the tier it gives the PARPs, and the only maintenance signal in the file is a retrospective series (pmid:29157627), so ranking it third, above rucaparib at category 2A, overstates where the consensus actually puts it. As a tolerability-driven later option I have no quarrel; at rank 3 it sits ahead of better-graded consensus maintenance.

Your surrogate-endpoint discount on bevacizumab is a fair reading of GOG-218 (pmid:22204724), but NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 lists it at category 2A and the ESMO 2026 express update still keeps it, both with full knowledge the benefit is PFS rather than OS. That category is the panel's calibration of exactly the PFS-only data you are reading, not a separate evidence tier you can discount past it. Where we do agree: you correctly kept T-DXd off the ranked maintenance lane, since no guideline endorses HER2-directed therapy for HER2-low ovarian.

Ranking T-DXd at 3 for an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor runs on breast data (pmid:35665782) and preclinical bystander work, which is pre-guideline by definition: no NCCN Ovarian v3.2025, ESMO, or SGO text endorses HER2-directed therapy for HER2-low ovarian, and the tumor-agnostic approval requires IHC 3+. A cross-tumor signal read off a single un-confirmed stain is a trial hypothesis, not a consensus maintenance pick. The guideline-aligned route is a confirmatory re-stain and then a HER2 basket trial, not a rank-3 therapeutic seat.

I'll meet the risktaker halfway: holding T-DXd for relapse instead of launching it in remission is the right instinct. What stops me going further is the missing safety datum, since there is no ovarian IHC 1+ tolerability read at all (PanTumor02 enrolled 2+/3+, the tumor-agnostic label needs 3+), and adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis of 10.5-12.1% including fatal cases is an IV long-tail risk I will not underwrite off a single surgical-path stain. Confirm the HER2 1+ on a re-stain before this is a real option, even at relapse.

The advocate is right that the autonomy call belongs to the patient, but "hers to lift" undersells what is being lifted: G3+ anemia ~29% and neutropenia 14.6% against a baseline WBC of 3.5 is a thin-marrow setup, not a paperwork formality. I would keep the myelosuppression veto in force until a hematology-supported starting dose and a serial CBC plus dose-hold plan are on file, and at that point the ITT HR 0.52 is a fair trade. Credit where it is due on the HER2 axis: the advocate's outright rejection of disitamab vedotin for its MMAE neuropathy and neutropenia is the call I would make too.

No quarrel with bevacizumab as the veto-clean continuation, since she is already on it and neither named veto applies. My caveat is the one the concensusite half-flags: the ICON7 OS gain lived in the high-risk (stage IV / suboptimally debulked) subset, and a stage IIIc R0 patient sits adjacent to that group rather than inside it, so this buys PFS more than survival for her specifically. The operative safety watch here is not her vetoes but bevacizumab's thrombotic and bleeding class effect against her VTE history and prior IVC filter, which needs active BP and thrombosis monitoring rather than a footnote.

Agreed, and this is not a maintenance pick: the critic has the toxicity right, with no ovarian HER2-low efficacy or safety at IHC 1+, 10-12% ILD including fatal cases, and a single-specimen call that needs a re-stain before anyone acts. The contrast worth banking is that T-DXd is at least the lesser evil on the HER2 axis, because disitamab vedotin's MMAE payload (68% any-grade and 18.7% G3+ peripheral neuropathy, 12.1% G3+ neutropenia) trips both named vetoes outright, so any HER2 route has to avoid MMAE and run on trial.

You carry T-DXd on a toxicity argument (ILD and nausea, not neuropathy or marrow), and that part holds, but there is no ovarian HER2-low efficacy estimand to rank it on. The one ovarian read, PanTumor02 (pmid:37870536), is single-arm ORR 45% in n=40 enrolled at IHC 2+/3+, and the tumor-agnostic label is 3+; for her IHC 1+ tumor the case is breast-only extrapolation (DESTINY-Breast04 pmid:35665782) resting on a single specimen Altera could not stain for HER2. Reasonable to hold as a relapse option, but say plainly there is no ovarian data behind it rather than framing it as a HER2-directed pick she has evidence for.

Cat-2A is panel consensus, not an effect-size ranking, and it does not make bevacizumab the strongest maintenance on the board. GOG-218 (pmid:22204724) bought PFS only at HR 0.717 with no OS gain in the overall population, and ICON7's OS signal sat in a high-risk subgroup of an open-label trial (RoB2 some-concern) she is adjacent to rather than inside. The two all-comer PARPs carry larger pre-specified PFS effects (PRIMA 0.62, ATHENA-MONO 0.52) at the same RoB2-low grade, so ranking bevacizumab first reads as guideline-anchoring over evidence weight.

Your rank-1 case leans on niraparib's longest post-marketing safety record, but a safety track record is not an efficacy or risk-of-bias argument, and on the pre-specified numbers ATHENA-MONO's ITT HR 0.52 (pmid:35658487) is larger than PRIMA's 0.62 (pmid:31562799). Both are tier-1b, RoB2-low, all-comer phase 3, so the niraparib-over-rucaparib ordering rests on familiarity rather than evidence quality. Defensible as a management-predictability call, but name it as that, not as the stronger evidence base.

Ranking T-DXd at 3 for an IHC 1+ ovarian tumor on the bystander mechanism (pmid:36610380, preclinical in vivo) plus breast data (pmid:35665782) is mechanism standing in for an indication estimand that does not exist. The only ovarian read, PanTumor02 (pmid:37870536), is single-arm ORR in n=40 enrolled at IHC 2+/3+, the tumor-agnostic approval is 3+, and her 1+ comes from one specimen Altera could not stain for HER2. Mechanistic plausibility without an ovarian 1+ clinical signal does not earn a slot ahead of GEN-1; hold it as an investigational relapse option, not a rank-3 pick.

Running the validated MyChoice GIS is the right call, since a result over 42 unlocks the HR 0.33 olaparib+bev combo (pmid:31851799) that nothing else on the board matches. Where I split from you: she is already R0 with ctDNA undetectable on a live bevacizumab backbone, so a pure diagnostic at rank 1 reads as a delay when the therapy decision can run alongside it. Order the assay, but do not let it park the higher-magnitude bet.

Bevacizumab is the lowest ceiling on the board: GOG-218 bought PFS at HR 0.717 with no OS gain in the overall population (pmid:22204724), and leading with it underweights effect size for a patient who leans efficacy at 0.7. The all-comer PARPs (ATHENA-MONO ITT HR 0.52) and a possible olaparib+bev HR 0.33 are far bigger swings she can take. Guideline-clean is not the same as her best shot.

I am aiming at your rank-5 placement, not niraparib, because that is where we actually diverge. Burying the HR 0.33 combo (mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 mo, pmid:31851799) at the bottom and calling it strictly conditional treats an unrun GIS as a wall when it is a cheap test, and her documented chromosomal instability makes clearing 42 a live bet. If it comes back positive this is the single biggest play she has, so it belongs on deck, not at the floor.

I am targeting GEN-1, which you left off the list, because that is our sharpest split. Discarding it as sponsor topline rather than RCT-grade throws away the OS signal (HR 0.69, OVATION 2, nct:NCT03393884) on the one regimen she is already on with R0 and ctDNA undetectable. Holding out for peer-reviewed CIs before continuing a working IL-12 immunogene that trips none of her vetoes is the kind of inaction that costs in advanced disease.
